author: potuz
content:
I do not see the circuit breaker as a form of penalty but rather as an easy way of quickly making sure the network is healed. I haven't read all this thread but I'm pretty sure someone must've replied this already: the chain doesn't really *need* every single builder to be able to cast a bid, so blacklisting temporarily one that has shown to miss a Payload is a preventive measure that still keeps liveness on the chain counting on every other builder alive. The "systemic" failure rates in which we fallback to self building should be considered more carefully cause those indeed affect the chain negatively. 

Notice also that the design I'm planning for Prysm (that proposal is by no means a proposal, specially for other clients, that proposal is what we will implement on Prysm) adds an immediate cost to exercising the fee option as well. 

As I mentioned in my reply to Nico on <#892088344438255616> , the biggest drawback is builders keeping the auction on a relay, cause this forces us to blacklist the full relay if a single participant fails, and also delays whitelisting them back. Builders should know that this will happen if participating in a relay, that any random failure from one known index in the relay will trigger blacklisting for all other indices

author: vladimir_ea
content:
perhaps it is worth mentioning what relays do:
- they run an auction
- they also validate all blocks by re-simulating them (which affords some protection to the network)
- there is an 'optimistic' mode, whereby a relay holds collateral from a builder and for any blocks with value below that collateral, the block validation is done in the background and does not delay the bid. 
- if any background validation fails, the builder is 'demoted' to non-optimistic mode
- on very rare occassions (possible a handful of times a year) an optimisitically submitted block wins and turns out to be invalid.
- if this happens the builder's collateral is used to pay the proposer what they would have received

builders do not currently do nay of this themselves because they submit via relays.

author: gd_0
content:
The circuit breaker makes sense to me overall. The thing I think is critical to get right is the threshold for it triggering.

One failure and you're out for the epoch is too restrictive imo. It leaves zero margin for error which just isn't realistic. 

Additionally, if relays sign with one key for all builders, one invalid block from any of them takes the relay down for the whole epoch. That makes optimistic relaying extremely hard to run, and would mean relays have to manage access to it heavily, e.g. only granting it to builders with months of clean history behind them.

With a bit more leniency, say 2 failures in an epoch, relays would be able to mitigate this. e.g.:
- First failure, switch everyone to non-optimistic
- Keep delivering blocks for the rest of the epoch, re-enable optimistic next epoch
